newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Megaworld profit growth seen tapering.
newsitem.headline: Megaworld profit growth seen tapering.

text.p: Megaworld Properties and Holdings Inc said on Wednesday it posted a 237 percent increase in net income in the first nine months of 1996 and analysts say its full-year prospects remain bright but not as spectacular as the boom years of 1994 and 1995.
Megaworld said its net income from January to September jumped to 2.086 billion pesos from the year-ago 619 million pesos.
But analysts said the figures include a 765-million pesos extraordinary gain from the initial public offering of Megaworld's mass housing unit, Empire East Land Holdings Inc.

Stripped of its extraordinary gain, Megaworld's profits from operations reached 1.321 billion pesos up 113 percent compared to the same period last year, said Erwin Balita, analyst at Dharmala Securities Phils Inc.
"The figures were slightly above expectations. Earnings prospects of the firm remained bright but not as spectacular as the past two years," said Balita.
Balita said it expects Megaworld to post a net income of between 2.2 billion and 2.3 billion pesos this year, including the 765-million peso extraordinary gain.
Brokers said Megaworld earlier forecast a 1.5-billion peso net income from operations this year.
Balita said Megaworld's net income from operations soared by 253 percent to 416 million pesos in 1994, and by 129 percent to 958 million pesos in 1995.
"I expect Megaworld to post a recurring net income growth of above 50 percent annually up to 1998," Balita added.
Cecilio Castro, analyst at Anscor Hagedorn Securities, said rising demand for low-end mass housing units would continue to drive up Megaworld's income.
"Empire East, Megaworld's mass-housing arm, would continue to contribute a hefty share to the bottom-line earnings of Megaworld," said Castro.
Balita said prospects of robust growth in the low-end property segment would more than offset Megaworld' exposure in the high-end segment.
Fears that the property boom in high-end residential and office units was over sent Philippine property stocks into a tailspin earlier this month.
The Philippine Stock Exchange's property sub-index hit a record high of 179.38 points on July 5, a 50 percent jump from the start of this year.
It corrected to 140.01 on October 15 but has since recovered and closed at 151.83 on Wednesday.

Megaworld vice president for corporate management Cirilo Manlangit said his firm's strong cash flow in the past nine months would spur the firm to pursue its growth targets even more aggressively during the remainder of 1996 and next year.
The firm's earnings prospect "continue to be bright considering that we have five big projects scheduled for completion this year," he said in a statement.
